findings.category: availability / same class of defect as A36-001: correlated subquery, quadratic in ONE account's own completed attempts, synchronous in node:sqlite (be/src/game.ts:1015-1018, Game.analytics, GET /api/classes/:id/analytics)
findings.evidence: Code: the 'clean first try' query of Game.analytics is `SELECT a.user_id,... FROM attempts a WHERE a.user_id IN (...) AND a.status='completed' AND a.started_at = (SELECT MIN(b.started_at) FROM attempts b WHERE b.user_id=a.user_id AND b.mission_id=a.mission_id AND b.status='completed')`. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN: `SEARCH a USING INDEX idx_attempts_active (user_id=? AND status=?)` / `CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY 1` / `SEARCH b USING INDEX idx_attempts_active (user_id=? AND status=?)`: mission_id is NOT in the index (db.ts:162), so for every outer row of mission M the subquery walks all of that user's earlier completed attempts (with a table lookup each) until it meets the first attempt of M. Cost = sum over missions of (attempts of M) x (attempts before the first attempt of M): quadratic when one account plays K attempts of mission A, then K of mission B. REPRODUCED through the real HTTP API (default code, only RATE_START_PER_MINUTE/RATE_ANSWER_PER_MINUTE raised to build the rows quickly; the rows are exactly what POST /missions/:id/start + /answer write): student 'Mal' joins teacher's class with the join code, plays 1500 x hem-01 then 1500 x hem-02 (3000 attempts): teacher GET /api/classes/1/analytics = 232 / 202 / 203 ms; 4000 x hem-01 then 4000 x hem-02 (8000 attempts, 14 MB db): 3648 / 3679 / 3612 ms, and a concurrent GET /api/health from another client was answered only after 3.64 s (event loop blocked). GET /classes/1/students (roster) 7 ms and /students/:id 6 ms at the same time: only analytics is affected. Synthetic rows with small result_json (db built by SQL, K then K attempts of hem-01/hem-02): 2000 / 4000 / 8000 / 12000 attempts = 76 / 292 / 1155 / 2505 ms (health stalled 1153 ms and 2496 ms). Extrapolating the quadratic (not measured): 20,000 attempts ~ 20 s per call. Same code with the EXACT same fixture shape but a well-behaved account (5000 attempts of a single mission, or 5000 spread over 10 missions) = 3-4 ms, and a class of 2000 students x 20 attempts = 354 ms (linear), so the trigger is one account's history shape, not the class size. DEMO_MODE=1 variant (self-triggered, no teacher needed): POST /api/auth/demo {role:student} gives Alex a passwordless token, POST /api/auth/demo {role:teacher} gives Dr Moreau's token; Alex plays 3000 x hem-01 + 3000 x mic-03 (both left over after the seeded story), then `GET /api/classes/1/analytics` as Moreau = 2105 / 2079 / 2092 ms per call, repeatable at will (same call after 3000+3000 attempts of missions Alex had already played in the seeded story: 35-44 ms, because the first attempt of each mission is then early in the index). Attack cost under DEFAULT limits, measured: an account creates 60 completed one-step attempts per minute (hem-01; 429 beyond that: start limit 60/min), 40/min on 3-step missions (answer limit 120/min); one-step missions hem-01, mic-02, mic-03, bio-02 are all reachable; there is NO cap on attempts per account. So ~4000 attempts = ~67 min, 8000 = ~2.2 h per account. Preconditions: the attacker is a member of the teacher's class (join code, 10 joins/10 min) and the teacher opens Faculty analytics (web/src/pages/faculty.tsx:73 calls analytics + roster on every open); each open then freezes the WHOLE API (login, answers, hints of every other user) for seconds and the time grows quadratically with no upper bound. Not in docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md (line 38 only documents the per-STUDENT linear cost of analytics).
findings.fix_hint: Replace the correlated MIN with one pass, like A36-001: `SELECT user_id, mission_id, wrong_total, hints_total FROM (SELECT a.*, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, mission_id ORDER BY started_at) rk FROM attempts a WHERE user_id IN (...) AND status='completed') WHERE rk=1` (RANK keeps the 'all rows tied on MIN' semantics), or JOIN on a GROUP BY user_id, mission_id MIN(started_at) subquery. A covering index (user_id, mission_id, status, started_at) would also make the MIN a single seek. Add a scaling test like r36-fixes.test.ts (1500 attempts of mission A then 1500 of B, analytics < 150 ms). Optionally cap completed attempts per account or per day.

findings.category: availability: unthrottled authenticated GETs with O(all students) cost; listed item (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS 'Scale', leaderboard 'no rate limit') understates the abuse case
findings.evidence: GET /api/leaderboard (be/src/game.ts:872-899) runs ~5 queries per student of the whole cohort plus SELECT id,name FROM users, and the route has no limiter (be/src/routes.ts, only answer/hint/start/write/join/login/register have one). Measured single call: 2000 students 35-46 ms, 3574 users 75-88 ms, class cohort of 2000 = 66 ms. One normal student account sending 20 concurrent GET /api/leaderboard?scope=all&cohort=all against the 2000-student database (992 requests in ~6 s, all 200): GET /api/health from another client p50 641 ms / max 1380 ms, another student's GET /api/dashboard p50 670 ms / max 2055 ms (baseline 3 ms / 20 ms). The same 20-connection flood on a cheap endpoint (/api/me, 11,511 requests) leaves health at 2-3 ms, so the amplification is the O(N) handler. Cost grows linearly with registered students (about 20 us per student per call), so 20,000 students would be ~0.4 s per call. The documentation calls this 'fine for the demo class of 38' but does not state that a single registered account can degrade every other user with ordinary requests; nothing in the code bounds it.
findings.fix_hint: Rate-limit authenticated GETs per account (e.g. leaderboard 10/min), and compute the leaderboard from a single aggregate query (SUM(best_score) GROUP BY user_id, xp_events window) with a short-lived cache keyed by (scope, cohort) instead of ~5 queries per student.

findings.category: availability / unbounded per-account data: Game.streak() loads every answer_log row of the account into JS (be/src/game.ts:602-609, called by GET /api/dashboard)
findings.evidence: streak() does `SELECT created_at FROM answer_log al JOIN attempts a ... WHERE a.user_id = ?` and builds a Set in JS: O(own answer_log rows), no LIMIT, no GROUP BY day. answer_log is capped at 400 rows per attempt (game.ts:404) but attempts per account are not capped, so rows are bounded only by the answer rate limit (120 answers/min = 7,200 rows/hour per account, measured). Measured on a db with one student of 2,500 attempts x 400 log rows (1,000,126 answer_log rows): GET /api/dashboard = 730 / 644 / 633 ms (all other endpoints of that account 2-10 ms; teacher roster 45 ms, student detail 42 ms), server RSS 103 MB -> 1,010 MB after 3 calls; 4 concurrent GET /api/dashboard from that account (126 requests in 4 s): health p50 2779 ms / max 3813 ms, another user's dashboard p50 2965 ms, RSS 1,525 MB. Linear: 100k rows ~65 ms. Time to build 1M rows by one account under default limits: ~139 h (7,200 rows/h), so this is P2 not P1; with N accounts each account's own dashboard is the amplifier (GETs are unthrottled, see A37-002). Not listed anywhere in docs.
findings.fix_hint: Compute the streak in SQL over distinct days: `SELECT DISTINCT created_at/86400000 AS d FROM answer_log al JOIN attempts a ... WHERE a.user_id=? AND created_at >= ? ORDER BY d DESC` (bounded by now - N days), or store last-activity days in a small table. Also cap attempts per account/day.

findings.category: unbounded in-memory structure: prepared-statement cache keyed by SQL text that embeds the class size (be/src/game.ts:101-106, 1011, 1015-1022)
findings.evidence: Game.stmt() caches every prepared statement forever in a Map keyed by the SQL string. Game.analytics() builds three statements with `WHERE a.user_id IN (?,?,...,?)` whose text depends on the class size, so each distinct class size ever analysed adds 3 native statements that are never finalised. Reproduced in-process (class grown 1..3000 members, analytics() called at each size): cached statements 1513 / 3013 / 4513 / 6013 / 9013 at sizes 500 / 1000 / 1500 / 2000 / 3000, RSS 208 / 422 / 760 / 1131 / 1270 MB (JS heap only 8-34 MB, so the memory is native sqlite3_stmt). For a normal class (<= 40 students) it is a few hundred KB; it only matters for a class that keeps growing while being viewed. The same pattern with competenciesOf() is bounded (<= 10 attempt ids). SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER (32766) would also make analytics answer 500 for a class larger than that (not tested).
findings.fix_hint: Do not cache statements whose SQL text varies (prepare + finalise on the fly for IN lists), or bind the ids as one JSON array (`WHERE user_id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))`), or bound the Map (LRU).

findings.category: correctness (display, P3): competency % uses floating-point sums, so exact .5 values round the wrong way, and the A36-001 rewrite changed the summation order
findings.evidence: Game.competencies() and competenciesOf() average `Math.max(0, 1 - 0.34*wrong - 0.15*hints)` floats and then Math.round(100*sum/n). Real API reproduction (fresh db): complete hem-01; start hem-02; step 1 correct first try; step 2 one wrong answer + one hint + correct; GET /api/competencies => {"name":"Pre-analytical quality","pct":75,"steps":2}. Exact value is (100 + 51)/2 = 75.5, which rounds to 76 (raw float 75.49999999999999). Exhaustive over pairs of steps (wrong 0..3, hints 0..3): 66 of 256 pairs display a different integer than the exact half-up rounding. Differential fuzz (see notes) also shows that the old (MAX subquery) row order and the new (RANK) row order sum the same rows in different orders: on 4 seeds x 400-700 random histories the displayed pct differs between old and new SQL for 14 / 24 / 27 / 29 users (about 1 user in 90, one competency off by exactly 1 point); 4+ values in one competency can already flip (e.g. [(1,2),(1,1),(1,1),(4,3)] -> 35 or 34 depending on order). So the A36-001 claim 'same result' holds for the selected ROWS (0 differences, see notes) but not bit-for-bit for the percentage, and the student result screen and teacher view (competenciesOf, another order) can differ by 1 point. No scoring/XP is involved.
findings.fix_hint: Sum integer hundredths (`Math.max(0, 100 - 34*wrong - 15*hints)`) and round half up on integers, in both competencies() and competenciesOf().

findings.category: unbounded per-account data: no cap on attempts / step_results per account (documented limit missing)
findings.evidence: Measured under default limits: one account completes 60 one-step attempts per minute (start limit 60/min, 429 beyond; 3-step missions 40/min). Each completed attempt stores ~1.8 KB (8000 attempts + 16000 step_results + 16000 answer_log = 14.4 MB database; result_json alone is 974 bytes), i.e. ~6.5 MB per hour and ~156 MB per day per account, with no cap per account, per day or for the database. Linear costs that grow with it: GET /competencies and GET /attempts/:id/result (competencies(), 11.6 ms at 5,000 attempts, 25 ms at 10,000, 65 ms at 20,000, 155 ms at 40,000: n log n, measured in-process on attempts with 3 solved steps), grantBadges scans (5,000 attempts: dashboard 14 ms). All other measured per-account endpoints stay under 20 ms at 5,000 attempts + 20,000 answer_log rows (dashboard, profile, badges, labs, lab lobby, vault, leaderboard x4, result, start, hint, answer, unlock, student detail, roster): no other superlinear handler found. With A37-001 and A37-003 this is what lets one account push other users' latency up; without a cap the only bound is time.
findings.fix_hint: Cap completed attempts per account per mission/day (or expire old attempts' step_results/answer_log), and document the limit in KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.
